summary: Saudi Arabia (Premium Residency, 2019; investor and property products from January 2024), Bahrain (Golden Residency, 2022; property route cut to BHD 130,000 in November 2025), Oman (Investor Residency Programme, 2021; relaunched as a 10-year Golden Residency at OMR 200,000 in August 2025) and Qatar (real estate residency from QAR 730,000 and the separate permanent residence card) all run residence, not citizenship, routes. Laws and fees are well documented for Saudi Arabia, Bahrain and Oman (gazette or official texts saved); Qatar's legal texts were blocked. Numbers are thin: only press statements and media relays of official figures, almost never split by investment route, and no revenue figures for any country.

events.title: State Audit Institution finds misuse of investor residence
events.description: The SAI's 2024 report summary finds that 378 workers in elementary occupations obtained investor residence after becoming 'business partners', that some foreign investors used facilities to get residence without real investment capacity, and that 52 investors left the commercial register without incentives being withdrawn (audit of the Investment Services Centre, 2022-2023). It is not clear whether these cases concern the long-term IRP or the general investor residence.

programs.name: Premium Residency (الإقامة المميزة; 'privileged iqama')
programs.notes: Residence without a Saudi sponsor, created by the Premium Residency Law (Royal Decree M/106 of 10/9/1440H, about 15 May 2019) and run by the Premium Residency Center. From 2019 two paid types: permanent for a one-time SAR 800,000 and fixed-term renewable for SAR 100,000 a year (fee-based, no investment required). Amended by Royal Decree M/84 of 11/6/1445H (published 10 Jan 2024): products and fees now set by the Council of Economic and Development Affairs; minimum age 21 removed. Five products added on 10 Jan 2024, including business investor (SAR 7 million invested over two years plus 10 jobs, permanent) and property owner (unmortgaged developed residential property worth at least SAR 4 million), each with a SAR 4,000 fee. Citizenship: the 2019 law said premium residency gave no right to Saudi citizenship (Art. 11(2)); the 2024 amendment repealed that sentence, but no path to naturalisation through premium residency is set out in the law. Official numbers are press statements and a figure attributed to the National Transformation Program.

programs.name: Golden Residency (الإقامة الذهبية)
programs.notes: 10-year renewable residence permit created by Minister of Interior Order No. 20 of 2022 (dated 10 Feb 2022; launched 7 Feb 2022). Categories: owners of property in Bahrain worth at least BHD 200,000 at purchase (cut to BHD 130,000 in November 2025), retirees with BHD 4,000 a month pension, long-serving employees (5 years, BHD 2,000 average salary) and retirees (15 years, BHD 2,000), and talents. Fee BHD 300 per person per 10-year permit (plus BHD 5 application fee now). Holder must be present at least 90 days a year. The property route is the only investment route. A separate 'platinum' residence (PM Resolution 47/2023) is for long-serving golden holders. No path to citizenship is stated. Official counts are press statements covering all categories together.

programs.name: Investor Residency Programme (إقامة مستثمر), relaunched in 2025 as the 10-Year Golden Residency
programs.notes: Launched by the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion on 29 Sep 2021 (applications from 3 Oct 2021). First category (10-year card): OMR 500,000 in a joint-stock company, government bonds or (from March 2022, Ministerial Decision 58/2022) residential property, or a company employing 50 Omanis. Second category (5-year card): OMR 250,000. Retirees also eligible. Visa and residence fees set by ROP Decision 234/2021 (OMR 500 / OMR 300, renewal every three years). On 31 Aug 2025 the ministry launched a '10-Year Golden Residency' with seven routes and a single OMR 200,000 minimum; its legal instrument and fees were not found, and it is not clear whether the 5-year category remains. Investors are 'not entitled to claim Omani citizenship, except under the existing regulations'. A separate owner residence for any property owner (no minimum in the text) was set by ROP Decision 87/2026.

programs.name: Real estate residency for non-Qatari property owners (الإقامة العقارية)
programs.notes: Under Law No. 16 of 2018 on non-Qatari ownership and use of real estate and Cabinet Decision No. 28 of 2020 (October 2020), a non-Qatari buying property worth at least QAR 730,000 in the designated areas gets residence for self and family without a sponsor for as long as the property is owned; from QAR 3,650,000 the owner also gets permanent-residency benefits (health, education, some business activities). Minimum stay of 90 days a year for certain categories (US State Department). Not a route to the permanent residence card or citizenship. Law texts not downloaded (Al Meezan blocked). No official count of permits found.

programs.name: Permanent Residence Card (Law No. 10 of 2018)
programs.notes: Not an investment programme: permanent residence after 20 years' legal residence (10 if born in Qatar), with income, good conduct and Arabic, plus listed categories (children and husbands of Qatari women, people with special services or qualifications). At most 100 people a year (Art. 4, per GLMM abstract). Holders are treated like citizens in state health and education and can own property and do some business without a Qatari partner. Included because the property route above grants 'permanent residency benefits' without the card. Law text not downloaded (Al Meezan blocked). No count of cards found.

gaps: Saudi Arabia: the Premium Residency Center's own product pages (saprc.gov.sa / sa.gov.sa) were blocked or did not resolve, so the 2024 product thresholds and the SAR 4,000 fee come from Argaam and Gulf News, not from an official text. The CEDA decisions setting product fees were not found.

Saudi Arabia: the original 2019 Umm al-Qura text of the law (Royal Decree M/106) and the 2019 CEDA fee decision (SAR 800,000 / SAR 100,000) were not downloaded; fees come from media. Whether these two original fees still apply after 2024 is not confirmed.

Saudi Arabia: the 8,074 permits for 2024 (with category split) are attributed to the National Transformation Program, but we did not find them in the NTP 2021, 2022 or 2025 reports or the Vision 2030 2023/2024 reports; the 2024 NTP report PDF was not located. No split by investor/property route, no revenue, no counts for 2020-2023.
Saudi Arabia: the 40,163 applications figure was reported by Saudi Gazette (site not reachable) without naming the official source.

Bahrain: the legal instrument that lowered the property threshold to BHD 130,000 in November 2025 was not found on lloc.gov.bh (scan of Interior Ministry orders 2022-2026 returned errors for most numbers). No official statistics series; counts are press statements (all categories together), none split by property route, no revenue figure.
Bahrain: the BNA original of the November 2024 'over 10,000 permits from 99 countries' statement was not retrieved; we used TradeArabia's relay.

Oman: the legal basis and fees of the August 2025 Golden Residency (OMR 200,000) were not found; it is unclear whether the 2021 IRP categories (OMR 500,000 / 250,000) were formally repealed. Texts of ROP and Housing decisions come from Qanoon.om, not the official gazette.
Oman: no count of cards issued after August 2023 and none for the Golden Residency; no figure on total investment after May 2022; no revenue figures.
Oman: the SAI audit finding on 'investor residence' does not say whether it concerns the long-term IRP or the general investor residence of foreign-investment-law company partners.

Qatar: Al Meezan (official legal portal) blocked us with a firewall captcha, so the texts of Law 10/2018 (permanent residence), Law 16/2018 (non-Qatari ownership) and Cabinet Decision 28/2020 were not downloaded or quoted from the original. No official count of real estate residencies or permanent residence cards issued was found. Our web search budget ran out before searching further for Qatari counts.

All four: no audit, parliamentary, IMF, FATF or EU document was found that gives numbers on these programmes (beyond Oman's SAI finding). None of these residence programmes leads to citizenship by investment.
